stance_basis: Duke defends adequacy of existing studies while committing to future ecological investigations for other projects
summary: Duke Power Company, as the project applicant, provides numerous corrections and clarifications to the DEIS throughout the document, generally defending the sufficiency of its environmental studies and mitigation measures. Duke maintains that its preconstruction botanical surveys are adequate and that further studies along access roads are not warranted, while acknowledging some environmental costs (e.g., loss of trout stream) as minor relative to project benefits. Duke also commits to cooperating with wildlife agencies and conducting future investigations for other planned projects.
complaint_summary: Duke acknowledges the loss of 2.3 miles of trout stream as unmitigable but characterizes it as a minor environmental cost relative to the project's benefits, and commits to cooperating with the state wildlife agency on trout management.

statement.text: Duke does not see a viable method to realistically mitigate the loss of the 2.3 miles of trout stream that will be inundated. This is a very minor cost to the environment considering the ast benefits of the project. However, Duke will cooperate with the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department regarding trout management plans for any of the streams on company lands.
